newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt steady, ahead of US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt steady, ahead of US jobs data.

text.p: Brady bond prices were mostly unchanged on extremely low volume on Friday ahead of the key U.S. employment report scheduled to be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT later today, traders said.

"I am quite surprised because it is still well bid. I thought it might have sold off a little bit into today's numbers but it seems to be very static and very similar to last night's closing prices," said one emerging market trader at a U.S. investment bank in London.
According to a Reuters poll, U.S. economists forecast 193,000 payroll jobs were created in July against 217,000 in June and a jobless rate of 4.9 percent.
Still, traders said market activity was nearly nonexistent although some Brady bond instruments were quoted higher in early London trade.

"The benchmarks are about where they ended last night and activity this morning has been virtually nil across the board. Everyone is on hold for the jobs report," said another trader at a European bank in London.
In the East European market, Russian dollar-denominated debt were bid 1/4 higher at 95-3/8 and Poland's par bonds were unchanged at 60-1/2 bid.

Among the Latin debt instruments, Argentine Brady bond instruments were quoted slightly higher on growing expectations the country would receive a credit ratings upgrade soon. Argentina is currently rated BB by Standard and Poor's Corp and B-1 by Moody's Investors Service Inc.
"People expect it to happen in the nearest future," said the trader at the European bank.
Argentine par bonds were 1/8 firmer at 76-1/8 bid and the country's discount bonds were 1/4 better at 90-3/8 bid. --Diane Craft, London Newsroon +44 171 542 5110
